To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the most common paths of Hypervisor attacks are: (1) a guest VM can attack the Hypervisor, (2) an external attacker can attack the Hypervisors, and (3) an internal attacker (i.e. cloud administrator) can attack the Hypersor.

(i) Hypervisors have been the subject of a large number of vulnerability reports, (ii) the most common attack vectors are related to memory management and privilege escalation, (iii) most of the attacks originate in the guest domain, and (iv) the most common targets are also the guest domain and the Hypervisor itself.

(1) Hypervisor vulnerabilities are mostly triggered by rogue guest VM's and remote attackers; (2) they are mostly caused by memory management and scheduling issues; and (3) most of them target the Hypervisor's own runtime domain.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the following questions: What Hypervisor vulnerabilities are out there?
understanding the security threats to which Hypervisors in cloud computing servers are exposed, and with characterizing Hypervisor Vulnerabilities.
the security of the Hypervisor, and the threats it is exposed to.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the Hypervisor Vulnerabilities are not a single entity, but rather a collection of vulnerabilities with different triggers, attack vectors, and targets.
the Hypervisor is a target for attackers and a weak point for the security of the cloud infrastructure.
the Hypervisor security problem is not only a problem of security, but it is a problem of complexity, as the Hypervisor has to deal with a large number of different security issues.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we have provided a systematic and detailed study of the Hypervisor security, and proposed a characterization that can be used to better understand the threats that Hypervisors face, and the potential paths that attackers may take to exploit them.

the Hypervisor is a critical component of a cloud server and it is exposed to a variety of attacks, which can be categorized into three dimensions, and the Hypervisor's vulnerabilities are mostly triggered by remote attackers.
Hypervisor vulnerabilities can be exploited by both remote and local attackers, and that most vulnerabilities are related to the Hypervisor's memory and device management functionalities.
The main takeaway from our work is that
, despite the fact that Hypervisors are designed to be secure and trusted computing bases, there are still many ways for attackers to compromise the security of the system.
the majority of vulnerabilities are triggered from within the guest VM, and the attack target is the Hypervisor itself.
, although Hypervisors may be exposed to attacks coming from different sources, the most common paths are triggered by rogue guest VM's.
